## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5039a6783f4f118e7cef8fb542e3621ec7c0c1ff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/untrusted-text.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-post-protocol.md + scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

- Read: the card body and both comments (claim 6895826066, os-dev-report 6896645434), the PR body and its 6-file list, the net diff `origin/main...5039a678` (merge-base 895783a1 = `main` at read time, 247 insertions, 38 deletions), and the head's check-runs. Outside the diff, read only to judge it: `recordAuthorTrusted` and `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` in `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, `RELAY_COMMENT_AUTHOR` in `ops.mjs`, the response handling of `fleet-write/execute.mjs`, and H72 in `check-half-states.mjs`.
- Check-runs on this head at read time: 17 completed `success` (Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · workspace / source gates / debt ledger, Test Core 2/8, among them), zero failures. ⚠️ Six still PENDING: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is the one that was red on the dev's first round (the line-pinned census); its verdict on this head is NOT in yet, and this record does not stand in for it. The rest are skipped by path filter.
- The dev's self-test counts (98 / 433 / 396) are the dev's local reading; this review re-ran nothing. The CI job that runs the tooling self-tests is green on this head.
- The diff matches its declared file surface exactly: six files, no file outside the claim.
- The PR carries items 1 and 2 of the card and is `Part of`, so the card stays open with item 3 and the one-off sweep (and its record on the card) still owed.

### ② Semver level

- No published package, schema or runtime path is touched: `scripts/pm/**` tooling and two `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**` lines. No changeset is owed; `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body agree with the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay-opened, attributed to `os-steve`), draft, base `main`. Not a fork. The governed surface (`.claude/**`) is in the diff, so the merge leg waits on a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval or this at-tier record; unchanged by this review.
- SQL push-down: n/a, no query path.
- Dev open question 1 (can the relay App still comment on a locked mailbox; NOT MEASURED): ANSWERED with a changed plan and ESCALATED, see S1. Option A as written is not enough, because step ⑤ locks every NEW mailbox from the moment of merge, before any sweep or canary runs.
- Dev open question 2 (item 3 left out): option A ACCEPTED. Item 3 guards one fleet seat writing another seat's signature through the relay; it needs relay access, which no outside account has, so it is not on the path this card closes. Its consumer is a board read, outside a pure reader. `Part of` keeps the card open. The follow-up card is owed by the lane seat and is not filed yet.
- Dev open question 3: the relay-side `pm:mailbox` fence is S2 (follow-up card, escalated to the lane seat); the un-lowered ratchet pin is nit N2.
- `security_findings: none` in the dev report: this review found no path by which an outside account passes the author fence.

### ④ Design judgment

Author fence (`record-recognisers.mjs`), tried against the card's goal:

- `readMailboxComment` judges `row.user.login`, the platform-stamped field, through `recordAuthorTrusted`: a string, non-empty, an exact `includes` in `[RELAY_COMMENT_AUTHOR, ...GOVERNED_APPROVERS]`. It never reads the signature line or any body text to decide. HOLDS.
- Spoofing: a missing row, missing `user`, a null `user` (a deleted account), an empty login, `objectstack-fleet` without the suffix, a trailing space, a case variant, and a seat account all read `ignored`. The match is exact and fails closed. A `[bot]` login cannot be registered by a user and App slugs are unique, so no second account can carry the relay's login; no `user.type` check is needed.
- Edited comment: the field read is the comment's creator, which an edit does not change. An outsider cannot edit a fleet or maintainer comment. An account with write access can edit one, but every such account is inside the fleet. HOLDS for the card's threat.
- The ignored body: it is never handed to `readMailboxLine`; the verdict is a two-key constant object, and `mailboxEvents` stamps only comment id, time and login onto it. H72 reads `events`, which no longer holds ignored rows, so the body cannot reach a printout. The self-test pins the marker absent. HOLDS.
- Limit, stated so nobody over-reads the fence: its one live consumer is H72 (report-only). A seat hears a knock as a PR-activity event from the harness, which this reader does not sit in front of. So for the session's context the LOCK is the gate and the fence is the rule plus the tooling reading. Until the sweep runs, every mailbox opened before this merge still takes outside comments. The sweep is load-bearing, not housekeeping.

Lock (`ops.mjs`, `validate.mjs`, `mailbox-open.mjs`):

- The row takes `issue` alone; a caller-sent `lock_reason` or any other key is refused; one PUT, body fixed by the table; `issues` is a literal grant so the mint widens nothing; no unlock row. The executor already lands a bodiless 204 as accepted for any row, so the lock's 204 (first or repeated) reads as a landing. HOLDS.
- `--lock N` reads the pull first, refuses unless open and `pm:mailbox`, and writes nothing when already locked. The open reads the pull back `locked: true` and exits non-zero naming the re-send when it is not. HOLDS.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — the unmeasured App-comment risk ships on the OPEN path, not only on the sweep. From merge, every new mailbox is locked at step ⑤ with no canary, and the relay has no unlock. If an installation token cannot comment on a locked conversation, each new mailbox is deaf at birth and each one needs a maintainer's hand to unlock. The failure would be loud (the knock's relay stroke fails) and bounded, and write-permission Apps are expected to pass, which is why this is not a must-fix; but it is cheap to remove entirely. Plan: BEFORE merge, a maintainer locks ONE existing mailbox by hand (one click, undone by the same hand), a seat sends one relay knock to it, and the stroke's result is recorded on the card. Landed: merge, then sweep every open `pm:mailbox` PR with `--lock N` and record the list on the card. Refused: do not merge step ⑤ as written. If the hand probe is not available, the first live act after merge is `--lock` on one mailbox plus one knock, before any seat opens a new mailbox. Escalated to the lane seat to ask the maintainer alongside the governed approval.
- S2 (should-fix) — `conversation_lock` can be aimed at any issue or pull; only the CLI caller fences on `pm:mailbox`. The dev's argument (a seat may already close any issue) misses one asymmetry: a close is undone through the relay, a lock is not, so a mistyped or injected number is a one-way act that only a maintainer reverses, and if S1's probe fails it also silences the relay on that thread. `mailbox_branch_delete` is the precedent for a fence in the executor on the executor's own read. A label fence stops mistakes, not a hostile seat (a seat can add the label first), so the security gain is modest. Disposition: a follow-up tooling card for the fence in `execute.mjs`, outside this card's surface; does not block this head.
- N1 (nit) — `mailboxEvents` returns `ignored`, and nothing prints it. A seat account that knocks directly instead of through the relay is now dropped without a word to anyone. A one-line count in H72 would make that visible.
- N2 (nit) — `seat-post-protocol.md` is at 87 under a pin of 88. The saving is not locked in until the pin drops.
- N3 (nit) — the sweep should also list outside-authored comments already on open mailboxes; they stay in the thread after the lock.

Skill text and ratchet:

- `untrusted-text.md` 54 → 54 and `seat-post-protocol.md` 88 → 87: lines in the family do not rise, each addition paid in its own file.
- Cut rule 1 (an internal PR adopting a fork diff waits for the maintainer's own approval) keeps its home in `external-contributions.md` ③, which states the rule itself. Cut rule 2 was a back-pointer sentence, not a rule; `seat-lifecycle.md` still points to this file.
- Both added lines agree with the code they teach: the two author sources by name, the reader by name, body not read. No issue number in either line.

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S1, S2), three nits.

**VERDICT: PASS**
